summary: Search cache rows and SERP snapshot histories are partitioned by the result-selecting context (proxy location, device, and result depth), and snapshot appends are exclusive.
reason: X-Proxy-Location and X-User-Agent change which results Serply returns but are not tenant headers, so the generated cache key ignored them. --num changes the retained list but was omitted from the snapshot identity, and an unlocked load-modify-rename dropped a concurrent run's history. The tools manifest must label those two fields as headers, matching the executable MCP bindings.
validated_outcome: Cache reads miss across location and device; snapshot paths differ by --num; eight concurrent appends all remain on disk.
